newsitem.title: USA: No new risk of Russian missile launch -U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: No new risk of Russian missile launch -U.S. official.

text.p: A senior Pentagon official said in response to a published report on Monday that he saw no increased risk of accidental or unauthorised launch of Russian nuclear missiles against the United States.

The official spoke in advance of Tuesday's start of two days of Washington talks between Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and top U.S. officials on bilateral military ties and security in Europe and the western Pacific.

"I have seen nothing to suggest to me that there is any reason to believe that there is a heightened risk of unauthorised or accidental launch" of Russian nuclear missiles, the official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters at the Pentagon.

The Washington Times said on Monday that a classified CIA report indicated recent malfunctions of equipment controlling Moscow's vast nuclear arsenal had spontaneously switched missiles to "combat mode" on several occasions, increasing the risk of unauthorised launch.
"I won't comment on our intelligence capabilities," said the official, who also refused to comment on any classified document.

"(But) I can tell you that I see nothing now that indicates a real level of concern in the Russian military, and I can tell you that I have seen nothing that indicates that any sort of an incident occurred," the official added.

Rodionov will hold separate talks on Tuesday with Defence Secretary William Cohen and White House National Security Adviser Samuel (Sandy) Berger, and meets on Wednesday with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright before departing for Hawaii and Japan.

The Pentagon official said the talks will centre on increased U.S.-Russian military cooperation, but will include Russian opposition to NATO enlargement. They will also include European security and the Pacific rim and the situation in North Korea, he said.

Reporters questioned the official at length about the Washington Times report, which comes in the wake of complaints by Rodionov in Moscow that Russian military forces are suffering from deep defence spending cuts.

Both the Washington Times report and the Pentagon official pointed out that even if a Russian strategic missile went into so-called combat mode, it would require special launch codes and authorisation from higher command authority to be fired.

The Times said the 13-page CIA report was based in part on statements from a former Russian officer in the Strategic Rocket Forces but did not specify when the alleged incidents occurred or how many missiles accidentally went on alert.
This week's visit will be Rodionov's first to the United States as defence minister and his first meeting with Cohen. Rodionov and former Defence Secretary William Perry met several times last year.
